A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoCoGaussian and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material and added efficiency study support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis experiments, component ablations, Gaussian-count experiments, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and adds measurements of GPU memory consumption and training time.

M1.justification: The CoC construction, adaptive Gaussian generation, weighting CNN, training objective, and optimization schedule remain unchanged. The new explanation of rendering sharp images using only base Gaussians is consistent with v1's Figure 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use Deblur-NeRF synthetic and real-world data, DoF-NeRF real-world data, and NeRF-LLFF. The added efficiency comparison uses the existing Deblur-NeRF real-world dataset without introducing a new task or input scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The new efficiency table measures the existing BAGS comparator on additional metrics; Mip-Splatting is named as a rendering-speed reference, without being separately evaluated against CoCoGaussian.

E3.justification: Appendix Section 13 adds an efficiency evaluation on Deblur-NeRF real-world data using an NVIDIA RTX 3090, reporting GPU memory and training time. Existing reconstruction metrics, data settings, and training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new efficiency analysis examines whether CoCoGaussian's computational costs are comparable to BAGS. Existing component ablations, Gaussian-count sensitivity experiments, reflective/refractive examples, luminance analysis, and CoC visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added efficiency measurements are also reported without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports 5.3 GB and 45 minutes for CoCoGaussian versus 4.7 GB and 47 minutes for BAGS. Rendering speed is described through equivalence to their underlying renderers. Existing numerical results in Tables 1-5 and the renumbered per-scene tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1-16, the ideal-lens assumption, the CoC diameter approximation, and the mathematical definitions of Gaussian generation and optimization remain unchanged. No new formal derivations or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about CoC-based reconstruction, robustness to unreliable depth, aperture/focus control, and state-of-the-art rendering quality. The efficiency addition supports the existing speed-oriented positioning.

C2.justification: New Appendix Section 13 interprets computational costs as comparable to BAGS and explicitly connects real-time feasibility to rendering only base Gaussians through 3DGS. Existing explanations of depth errors, luminance effects, and limitations when CoC diameter is underestimated remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds concrete training-time and GPU-memory information tied to a named dataset and RTX 3090, plus an explicit explanation of inference costs. Appendix Section 8's architecture, hyperparameters, training schedule, and the project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds a Mip-Splatting citation for the efficiency table. The introduction and related work also foreground DoF-NeRF's prior use of CoC and its rendering-speed limitations, a relationship already discussed in v1's Appendix Section 9.

P1.justification: There are localized introduction and related-work edits, a new efficiency subsection, updated affiliations, an internship footnote, and acknowledgements. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds efficiency Table 6, renumbers the existing per-scene tables from 6-8 to 7-9, and adjusts Figure 1's sizing and surrounding layout. Existing figure content and result-table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 supplements v1's qualitative speed assertions with a concrete resource comparison on specified hardware and makes the existing relationship to DoF-NeRF more visible. These additions improve transparency while preserving the original evidence. The gain is limited because Table 6 provides no numerical rendering-speed measurements and the method and reconstruction results remain unchanged.
